paragraphs.starts: Rules revision 73. A first draft
paragraphs.pictured: A working draft taken from a simulator, with placeholder content
paragraphs.confused: Talks about a 'friction table', a simulator and code. A player wouldn't know what these are.
paragraphs.weird: A rulebook that says the simulator wins when it disagrees with the rules files. It also says every number is a candidate.

paragraphs.starts: 1. The game in brief
You and up to three other players are good AIs
paragraphs.pictured: A co-op game for 1-4 players. Agents work like explorers, nodes like presence, ambassadors are our pieces.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Reads like Spirit Island: spirits against invaders. I'd assume agents behave like explorers and ravage. Here agents mostly just gather and corrupt sites.

paragraphs.starts: You win by the purge
paragraphs.pictured: Like Spirit Island fear: Unity tips lower the win bar. There are three ways to lose.
paragraphs.confused: 'Tipped 6 times' doesn't yet tell me how big a tip is.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Unity looks exactly like fear and terror levels, but the thresholds count tips (0-2/3-5/6+), not cards earned. A no-nodes loss is like a spirit losing all its presence, and the event deck running out is like the invader deck running out, so that matches.

paragraphs.starts: Each round the adversary acts first
paragraphs.pictured: Adversary, then draft, then a simultaneous action phase, then production, threats and war
paragraphs.false_familiarity: In Spirit Island the spirits grow and play first, then the invaders act. Here the adversary goes first every round and there is no fast/slow split. I'd keep thinking I can react before it moves.

paragraphs.starts: There is one country per player
paragraphs.pictured: 4x4-ish tiles of hexes, each also a megacorp
paragraphs.confused: How do 16 hexes make a 'square piece'? I need a diagram.

paragraphs.starts: A hex is city, open land or ocean
paragraphs.pictured: Cities, open hexes, some industrial zones, coastal cities
paragraphs.weird: A city can be 'printed as coastal' without touching ocean. That's an exception.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: In Spirit Island the ocean is a playable land for some spirits. Here no piece ever enters ocean, and ocean also blocks movement and reach targets.

paragraphs.starts: Two hexes are adjacent if they share an edge
paragraphs.pictured: 'Next to' means range 0-1. Ties go to the lower hex number.
paragraphs.weird: Adjacency crosses borders, but §10 corruption only counts adjacent hexes in the site's own country. That one exception is buried later.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: 'Next to' includes the hex itself. In Spirit Island 'adjacent' excludes the land itself, so I'd read 'next to' as excluding it.

paragraphs.starts: Cities, research stations and factories are sites
paragraphs.pictured: Three site types, each with an owner cube
paragraphs.weird: It has to warn that 'building' is a card and not a piece. That shows the term clashes.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: In Spirit Island, 'building' means an invader town or city. They headed that off, but I'd still say 'building' at the table and mean a board piece.

paragraphs.starts: Owner | City | Research station | Factory
paragraphs.pictured: A 3x3 grid of what each site produces for each owner
paragraphs.confused: 'Sells its 1 energy': at what price? (5 credits, found only in §12.) Where do the neutral cubes go, and what's a megaproject so far?
paragraphs.weird: A neutral factory makes nothing but corp troops at a Discord tip. Odd.

paragraphs.starts: Every city also builds a factory each round
paragraphs.confused: Where? It is only explained in §12.
paragraphs.weird: Every city builds a free factory every round, even corrupted ones. That's a lot of board growth for a one-line rule.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: It feels like the invader Build step, but every city builds a factory every round, and the owner can be a player.

paragraphs.starts: A front is a long edge shared by two country pieces
paragraphs.pictured: Borders with a pile of corp troops on each side
paragraphs.confused: Can a node or an ambassador stand on a base hex? (Move allows bases. Nodes aren't stated.)
paragraphs.weird: A base 'is not a site' but sits on an open hex.

paragraphs.starts: Node | a player | where you act from
paragraphs.pictured: Nodes, ambassadors, agents, botnets, two troop kinds, cubes, markers, tokens
paragraphs.confused: What's the difference between a corruption marker and land corruption? Only part of it is explained here.
paragraphs.weird: There are three different corruption-like things (corrupted site, marker, land corruption).
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Only one node per hex, of any player. Spirit Island lets presence stack and spirits share lands. Markers look like blight but don't cascade.

paragraphs.starts: Some cards hold their own tokens
A hex is in reach if it is on or next to one of your nodes
paragraphs.confused: With 'in one country', does any country include ones where I have no node? It says yes.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Spirit Island powers have different ranges, often from sacred sites. Here range is always 1. I'd go looking for range numbers on cards.

paragraphs.starts: Lay out the map
paragraphs.pictured: Tiles laid out for the player count

paragraphs.starts: In each country (each piece prints these places)
paragraphs.pictured: One corrupted city, one corrupted station with a botnet, a neutral station, two neutral factories
paragraphs.confused: No agents or troops start on the board?
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Spirit Island setup puts invaders on the board and does an explore. Here only cubes and a botnet start out. I'd want to pre-place agents.

paragraphs.starts: The adversary: its agent supply is 24 per country
paragraphs.pictured: Event deck stacked by stage, top card face up, agents in the pools
paragraphs.confused: '1 agent a country at the base difficulty'. Does that already include Garrisons' +1 (§10), or is it 1 + 1? Also what are the project slots?
paragraphs.false_familiarity: The stage-stacked deck is like the invader deck. But the top card is face up, unlike the face-down explore card.

paragraphs.starts: Shuffle the Unity deck
Each player takes an AI board, in this order
paragraphs.pictured: Fixed boards by seat. Place the first node, take 1 ambassador and 3 energy, claim a home city.
paragraphs.confused: Is '+1 insight' a one-off gain, or a lasting bonus that makes round-1 insight 6? It's wasted if one-off, since insight is set at round start. 'Nearest': counted in hexes, across ocean? No starting cards?
paragraphs.weird: You don't choose your board, the seat decides it.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Spirit Island lets you pick any spirit. Here the seat decides. I'd want to pick freely.

paragraphs.starts: The game starts with the adversary's turn
paragraphs.pictured: Adversary turn 1 before we have cards
paragraphs.false_familiarity: In Spirit Island the spirits act first in turn 1. Here the adversary deals threats and rallies before we even have cards.

paragraphs.starts: Round start | Your insight is set
paragraphs.confused: Production (E) comes before threats (F). So harm lands after income, and you can't use this round's income to pay.
paragraphs.weird: Sway (A) is its own step just for land corruption.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: No fast/slow and no separate ravage/build/explore. The adversary's whole turn is one step. Threats resolve after production, which is unlike Spirit Island's fear and events.

paragraphs.starts: After every action and every step, check in this order
paragraphs.pictured: A state-based check after every action
paragraphs.confused: Losing is checked before the purge. So if both happen at once, we lose?
paragraphs.weird: Holding Discord off comes before tipping. That reads like a patch for timing.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: In Spirit Island, victory is checked at set points and fear cards resolve at the fear step. Here everything is checked after each action.

paragraphs.starts: Nothing has a holding limit
Credits | yes | board income
paragraphs.pictured: Eight resources, two of them not kept
paragraphs.confused: 'Chips can't be sold' suggests other resources can be. Can anything besides cards be sold?
paragraphs.weird: Eight resources is a lot. Antimatter is only for tier-2 cards.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Energy is kept between rounds, just like Spirit Island energy. Fine.

paragraphs.starts: Insight is this round's attention
paragraphs.confused: How do I track which of my unspent insight came from another player (Patience)?
paragraphs.weird: 'Not insight another player gave them' is a carve-out bolted on.

paragraphs.starts: Insight comes at the start of the round
paragraphs.pictured: Most income arrives at the end of the round
paragraphs.confused: The §6 table lists '5 insight' as board income. Is it at round start or in upkeep? (Round start.)
paragraphs.weird: City energy and factory chips come 'earlier in production'. Two timings for income.
paragraphs.false_familiarity: In Spirit Island you gain energy at the start of your turn during growth. Here credits and energy come at the end, so round 1 is spent on starting resources only.

paragraphs.starts: Each player is one AI board
paragraphs.pictured: A player board with eight powers

paragraphs.pictured: Three boards with different incomes and slots

paragraphs.confused: Vigil: 'your node's hex', meaning any of the Protector's nodes? Can a troop born on a Wall hex strike neighbours or leave?

paragraphs.false_familiarity: Feels like a defend or Dahan-protection ability, but it only works against adversary troops, not corruption.

paragraphs.starts: Your nodes start on your board, on two tracks
paragraphs.confused: The track spaces aren't listed (which space gives what).
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Strongly Spirit Island. I'd assume the 'card-play track' raises how many cards I can play a round. No card-play limit is stated anywhere, so it can't do that.

paragraphs.starts: Every placement pays two prices
paragraphs.pictured: Power cost plus the energy shown on the space
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Spirit Island track numbers are what you GAIN once uncovered. Here they are a COST to uncover. I'd read 0,0,0,1,2,3,5 as energy income.

paragraphs.pictured: Range 1, an empty hex, no marker or land corruption
paragraphs.confused: Can it go on a military base hex?

paragraphs.starts: A lost node leaves the game
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Close to Spirit Island destroyed presence. Fine.

paragraphs.starts: Each power can be used once a round
paragraphs.false_familiarity: These aren't innate powers. There are no element thresholds. They're paid activations.

paragraphs.starts: Every board has Deploy
paragraphs.confused: Peer Review costs 3 cubes and the track's energy as well?

paragraphs.starts: The Protector's Bulwark

paragraphs.pictured: Programs stay, buildings go in slots, events are discarded
paragraphs.false_familiarity: Spirit Island cards are discarded and reclaimed. Here programs and buildings stay forever and their tags count permanently, unlike elements that count only this turn.

paragraphs.false_familiarity: Tags = elements, but they're permanent and countable

questions.question: Do any agents or troops start on the board at setup, like Spirit Island's initial explorers and towns?
questions.answer: No. Only adversary cubes on the marked city and station, plus a botnet. Agents wait in each country's pool (1 each at base difficulty) and land at the first Rally.

questions.question: How much insight do I have in round 1?
questions.answer: 5 from the board, plus 1 from the first economy space I uncovered = 6. (Assuming the '+1 insight' is the space's lasting bonus.)

questions.question: In a 2-player game, which boards are used?
questions.answer: Builder and Protector. No Researcher.

questions.question: Do we get cards before the adversary's first turn?
questions.answer: No. The adversary's turn (threats, rally, and so on) comes first, then the opening deal in step C, then the action phase where we can pay those threats.

questions.question: Can I use this round's upkeep income to pay a threat before it fires?
questions.answer: No. Paying happens only in the action phase. Production and upkeep (E) come after it, and threats fire in F.

questions.question: Spirit Island habit: can I hold a 'slow' card until after the adversary acts?
questions.answer: No. There's no fast/slow. The adversary's turn comes before the action phase every round. Anything you hold waits until after next round's adversary turn.

questions.question: After I pass, can I still sell a card or add to a threat?
questions.answer: No. When you pass you are done for this action phase.

questions.question: Does a Shelter used this action phase protect against corruption in next round's adversary turn?
questions.answer: No. It lasts 'this round' and ends at Cleanup (H). It covers threats (F) and war (G) this round. Even then, a node on a war-destroyed factory dies unless the stage-I last-node rule applies.

questions.question: Can insight I gain during the adversary turn (Vigil) be spent this round?
questions.answer: Yes. Insight is set at round start, and anything gained afterwards is usable until the next round start (when it's lost, except for the Researcher).

questions.question: Can I place a node on a hex with agents, or on a corrupted city?
questions.answer: Yes, both are allowed. Not on a hex with a node, a corruption marker or land corruption, and not on ocean.

questions.question: Spirit Island habit: can my node share a hex with another player's node, or can I stack two of mine?
questions.answer: No. One node per hex, of any player.

questions.question: My ambassador already stands on a neutral factory. Does it count toward the 3 for Claim?
questions.answer: No. Standing ambassadors don't help pay a claim. They do pay first for a Liberate.

questions.question: Does a botnet on a corrupted station stop me liberating it? Is the station then mine?
questions.answer: The botnet doesn't stop the Liberate and stays on the station. The station becomes neutral, not mine, and I can't then Claim it while the botnet is on or next to it.

questions.question: Can I Move an ambassador onto an open hex next to my node that has no site, base or node?
questions.answer: No. Move goes only onto a site, base or node in reach. (Remove agents can put one onto any hex in reach that has agents.)

questions.question: Who takes the harm from an unpaid threat?
questions.answer: The player whose node is closest to one of its tokens, however far. Ambassadors don't count for this. Tied players choose.

questions.question: Can a player with no node or ambassador near a threat chip in credits?
questions.answer: No. Only players near it (a node or ambassador on or next to a token) may pay or use a card on it.

questions.question: At stage III, can a threat destroy my last node?
questions.answer: No. A threat never takes a last node, at any stage.

questions.question: We put 4 credits on a 6-credit threat and couldn't finish. Do we lose the 4?
questions.answer: No. Payments on an unpaid threat return to their payers when threats take effect.

questions.question: At difficulty 1, does a '2 Security tags' counter become 3?
questions.answer: Not stated. The rule says '+1 on each non-credit item'. My guess is yes, tags count as a non-credit item.

questions.question: At 0-2 Unity tips, do agents waiting in the pools stop the purge?
questions.answer: Not stated clearly. The table says 'on the board', and pools seem to be off-board. My guess: no, only placed agents count.

questions.question: At 6 Unity tips, a corrupted station and land corruption remain but no corrupted cities. Do we win?
questions.answer: Yes, immediately. Corrupted stations, factories and land never count.

questions.question: Spirit Island habit: can an adversary troop attack my node or my aligned city?
questions.answer: No. Its only targets are player-owned research stations and factories.

questions.question: In a stage-II round, can a Corrupt line destroy my last node and lose us the game?
questions.answer: Yes. The last-node protection holds only while the card is stage I, unless I have Sanctuary or an ambassador guard. A player with no nodes loses the game for everyone. (The 'Losing nodes' paragraph doesn't name corruption explicitly.)

questions.question: If we spend swayed Unity to hold Discord off, does it also count toward the Unity tip?
questions.answer: No. Unity used to remove Discord doesn't go onto the Unity track. Only the rest does.

questions.question: When Discord tips with 2 over, does the overflow carry over? When do we lose to Discord?
questions.answer: No carry-over: Discord empties. (Unity keeps its extra.) We lose when a Discord tip finds the 6-card Discord deck empty, so on the 7th tip (the 6th at difficulty 4).

overall:
1. Node track numbers are costs, not income (0,0,0,1,2,3,5 energy to uncover). Spirit Island veterans will misread them. The 'card-play track' suggests a play limit that doesn't exist. Say both outright.
2. The order of play is the reverse of Spirit Island: the adversary goes first every round, there's no fast/slow, and threats fire after production. A one-page turn diagram with when you can respond would help most.
3. There are too many exception riders: Remove agents doesn't cancel, standing ambassadors pay for Liberate but not Claim, war kills nodes despite Shelter, guarding by a site owner except during corruption, Onyx once a round, Patience versus given insight, and per-troop versus per-source Effects. Group them, or cut them.
4. Two different agent counts: Corrupt X counts adjacent hexes in its own country only, natural corruption counts only the site's own hex. Plus 'next to' including the hex itself. Use the same terms throughout and show an example.
5. Holes: can land corruption be removed, does corruption take a last node at stage II+, do pools count for the purge, does a difficulty increase apply to tag counters, how do project slots and ongoing projects work, and 'cordon' appears only in the legend.
6. The difficulty tables look arbitrary: agent income goes 1→4, compute goes 3,4,18,24,13, and it's unclear whether Garrisons is included. Explain the curve or smooth it.
7. Liberated sites become neutral, not yours. That should be shouted, since 'liberate' implies taking the site back for us.
